title: These 9 Thunderbird features made me ditch Gmail for good
summary: The underdog with cooler and better features
body: At the beginning of this year, I decided to ditch Gmail for the first time in about 15 years. It was not my plan to let down Google’s email app, as I have always enjoyed features such as Proofread, Confidential Mode, and Undo Send ( this one saved me once when I almost sent an email meant for my wife to my boss). But that does not mean it’s the best option for everyone. Over time, the Gmail app stopped feeling like a tool for sending and receiving emails and became like a marketer trying to sell me Google’s services. From the push for smart features that I don’t need to ads and the cluttered, AI-supported interface, checking my emails became a chore.

title: Lenovo Smart Clocks are finally getting their weather back
summary: No more having to check outside like a sucker!
body: TL;DR Across August and September, Lenovo Smart Clock Essential owners reported losing the weather display on their devices. Within the past 24 hours, weather suddenly seems to be retuning. Change can be hard for smart homes. While we love getting new features that make our smart home hardware better, far too often we hear about manufacturers abandoning old products , turning off necessary cloud infrastructure and leaving them worthless. Even when they don’t break something entirely, sometimes old functionality just up and vanishes — like we learned about last month with the Lenovo Smart Clock Essential. Thankfully, today we have some good news to share for a change. Lenovo’s Smart Clocks are a lot more restrained than a full-featured smart home display like a Nest Hub, and the display on the Lenovo Smart Clock Essential focused on just showing you the time — and the weather. But this past summer, users started noticing that the weather was disappearing from their Smart Clocks , leaving only the time behind.

title: YouTube is cleaning up one of the worst parts of Shorts
summary: Giving low-effort Shorts less room to breathe.
body: TL;DR YouTube is updating Shorts recommendations to prioritize original content and reduce the reach of low-effort reuploads from other creators. Reused clips can still surface if creators add meaningful commentary, editing, storytelling, or another original angle. For viewers, the change should make the Shorts feed feel less repetitive, while creators clipping their own long-form videos likely won’t be affected. YouTube Shorts have never exactly been a fan-favorite feature. From users wanting Shorts to be a standalone app, to YouTube itself letting users set their daily Shorts feed limit to zer o, there’s no shortage of signs pointing to how unhappy many users are with how aggressively short-form video has been pushed across the platform. One of the big reasons behind the disdain is the sheer amount of slop that floods the Shorts feed . YouTube knows that, and it is now starting to prioritize original content on Shorts. Announced by the streaming giant in a blog post this week, YouTube is updating its recommendation system specific to Shorts to reduce the reach of re-uploaded content, where videos taken from other creators are reposted without adding anything meaningful.

body: An engineering model of NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) descent probe passed a key test that ran from Aug. 28 to Sept. 10, showing it can survive the extreme temperatures of Venus. NASA/Mike Guinto The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI team put the yoga ball-sized vessel into a ceramic-lined chamber with heat-scorched walls and ratcheted up the temperature to 869 F, or 465 C, over the course of about an hour — the same pace the probe will heat up during its descent to the surface of Venus. body: TL;DR A federal judge has ruled in Google’s favor in separate lawsuits brought by Chegg and Penske Media Corporation over AI Overviews in Search. Ed-tech company Chegg filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google last year over AI Overviews and how the feature was affecting website traffic and affiliate revenues. Publisher Penske Media Corporation, known for publications like Billboard , Variety , and Rolling Stone , later filed its own lawsuit against the search giant . title: A real ChatGPT page is being used to trick people into installing malware
summary: The dangerous part only appears after ChatGPT has already earned your trust.
body: TL;DR Attackers created a fake ChatGPT model called “Plus 5.6” on the real ChatGPT website. It sent users to a fake security check that tricked them into running a malicious Windows command. That command could install malware that could access files, the screen, the webcam, the microphone, and more. There was a time when spotting a sketchy download meant looking for misspelled websites, strange pop-ups, and other obvious red flags . But that gets much harder when the scam starts on a website you already trust. Security researchers have uncovered a malware campaign that does exactly that, using a real ChatGPT page to convince people they’re dealing with an official OpenAI product before redirecting them to a far more dangerous site. Researchers at Huntress (via TechRadar ) found attackers abusing ChatGPT’s Custom GPT feature to create a bot called “Plus 5.6.” The name was chosen to sound like an official OpenAI model, and because Custom GPTs are hosted on ChatGPT.com, anyone opening the link would see a legitimate ChatGPT address in their browser.
